title: libpod: switch sqlite state backend to WAL mode
body:
Fixes #29721

Under heavy container churn, the SQLite state DB can get corrupted with "database disk image is malformed" due to page 1 freelist header conflicts under the default rollback journal mode (#29721).

To address this:

Enable WAL Mode: Set _journal_mode=WAL in the SQLite connection string on local filesystems. This avoids writing directly to page 1 on every transaction and relies on SQLite's shared-memory locking.

Clean Truncation: Run a best-effort PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) on SQLiteState.Close().

Network Filesystem Detection: Added isNetworkFilesystem() pre-check. SQLite WAL mode requires POSIX mmap for -shm sidecar files, which network filesystems do not support. On Linux, we inspect unix.Statfs magic numbers (NFS, CIFS, SMB, AFS); on FreeBSD, we check unix.Statfs type prefixes (nfs, smbfs, afs). If a network filesystem is detected, WAL mode is bypassed automatically to keep the database fully operational.

Runtime Fallback Verification: Added verifyJournalMode() post-open query (PRAGMA journal_mode;). If WAL mode was requested but SQLite silently kept delete mode (e.g., FUSE-over-NFS mounts), log an informational warning and continue safely in rollback mode instead of failing.

Unit Tests: Added regression tests verifying WAL mode enablement (TestSqliteJournalModeWAL), silent fallback handling (TestSqliteVerifyJournalModeFallback), and local directory detection (TestIsNetworkFilesystemLocalReturnsFalse).

```release-note
Switched SQLite state database to WAL (Write-Ahead Logging) mode to prevent database corruption under high concurrency, with automatic fallback for network filesystems.```

Alright, so I went a little deeper on a quest to find out why we disabled WAL mode in the first place. We turned it off in https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/pull/18519 because of issues with the go-sqlite driver noted in https://github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3/issues/274 (issues which have long since been fixed). We've also subsequently raised the timeout for taking locks to 100 seconds from 5. Finally, we turned off shared cache in https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/pull/17889 which was also causing DB locked errors.

In short: there is no reason not to enable WAL mode in my mind.

One potential note of concern, though. Apparently WAL mode doesn't work on NFS - which could break some folks, because while Podman storage on NFS is unusual, it's not entirely unheard of. We may need a fallback to continue to use the current backend if database creation fails.

libpod/sqlite: add NFS fallback for WAL mode

SQLite WAL depends on POSIX mmap for its -shm file, which isn't supported properly on NFS. Because of that, Podman can fail when the storage root is on NFS without making the actual cause obvious.

The idea is to handle this in two layers:

Check statfs() before opening the DB. If the database directory is on a known network filesystem like NFS, CIFS, SMB, or AFS, don't enable WAL in the DSN in the first place.
After opening the DB, read back PRAGMA journal_mode. go-sqlite3 doesn't necessarily return an error when switching to WAL fails; it can just keep the previous journal mode. Reading it back lets us catch cases that the initial statfs() check can't detect, such as FUSE mounted over NFS.

If the journal mode doesn't match what we requested, log a warning and continue. SQLite can still work using the regular rollback journal mode.

The filesystem detection is kept OS-specific to avoid messing with build tags: Linux uses Statfs_t.Type and its filesystem magic numbers, while FreeBSD uses Fstypename.
